claims.text: Refractory high-entropy alloys can provide enhanced catalytic activity toward HER and HOR.
Refractory high-entropy alloys can provide enhanced durability toward HER and HOR.
The enhanced HER and HOR performance of RHEAs is due to their unique microstructure and composition.
The investigated RHEAs have nominal compositions AlxCoCrFeNi with x = 0.1, 0.75, or 1.5.
Al, Cr, and Si are added to the RHEA composition.
The proposed effect occurs in a high-temperature environment.
Adding appropriate amounts of Al, Cr, and Si to RHEAs forms a dense oxidation film on the alloy surface at high temperature.
The dense oxidation film improves the high-temperature oxidation resistance of RHEAs.
Improved high-temperature oxidation resistance enhances catalytic activity toward HER and HOR.
Improved high-temperature oxidation resistance enhances durability toward HER and HOR.
Al-, Cr-, and Si-modified RHEAs will outperform traditional HER and HOR alloys in catalytic activity and durability.
The exact mechanism connecting Al, Cr, and Si additions to HER and HOR performance is not fully understood.

contradictions.description: The nominal AlxCoCrFeNi compositions already contain Al and Cr, while the intervention describes adding Al and Cr as though they were absent. The intervention also adds Si, but no Si-containing modified composition or concentration is specified.
